article.title: Quinolinic acid contributes to maladaptive kidney injury and acute kidney injury-to-chronic kidney disease transition.
article.abstract: The transition from acute kidney injury (AKI) to chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains a major clinical problem with unclear underlying mechanisms. Emerging evidence suggests that alterations in tryptophan metabolism, particularly in the production of downstream metabolites such as quinolinic acid (QA), play a role in renal pathophysiology. QA, an intermediate in de novo nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide biosynthesis, is metabolized by quinolinate phosphoribosyltransferase (QPRT). We investigated whether QA contributes to kidney injury using models of folic acid-induced AKI-to-CKD transition and cisplatin-induced AKI, genetic and exogenous approaches to alter QA, and clinical observations. Untargeted kidney metabolomics identified QA as one of the most elevated metabolites after folic acid injury. After folic acid injury, Qprt haploinsufficiency exacerbated kidney injury and fibrosis-related gene expression; aged Qprt-haploinsufficient mice exhibited increased fibrosis-associated gene expression without overt renal dysfunction. Exogenous QA administration increased serum creatinine in uninjured mice and worsened renal dysfunction and fibrosis-related gene expression in the folic acid AKI-to-CKD model. Conversely, mice deficient in either 3-hydroxyanthranilate 3,4-dioxygenase (HAAO) or kynurenine 3-monooxygenase (KMO), which reduce flux toward QA, showed improved renal outcomes after folic acid injury and cisplatin-induced AKI. Multimodal spatial metabolomics analysis of kidney biopsies from patients with AKI revealed QA accumulation in regions of inflammatory infiltration. Last, children with CKD exhibited higher urinary QA compared with healthy individuals. These findings underscore QA as a potential mediator of kidney injury and a therapeutic target for preventing the progression from AKI to CKD.

score.summary_kr: 본 연구는 급성신손상(AKI)에서 만성신질환(CKD)으로의 전환 메커니즘을 규명하기 위해 퀴놀린산(QA)의 역할을 조사했습니다. 동물 모델(엽산 유발 AKI-to-CKD, 시스플라틴 유발 AKI)과 유전학적 접근(QPRT, HAAO, KMO 유전자 조작)을 이용하여 신장 대사체학 분석을 수행했으며, 신손상 부위에서 QA 축적을 확인했습니다. 최종적으로 소아 CKD 환자에서 요중 QA 수치가 정상인보다 높음을 보여, QA를 AKI-to-CKD 전환의 치료 타겟으로 제시했습니다.
key_points: 만성대사질환(CKD) 발병 메커니즘 규명을 위한 멀티오믹스(대사체학) 적용
동물 모델 × 유전학 × 임상 샘플(환자 신생검)의 통합 접근
질병 진행 예측 바이오마커(urinary QA) 발굴을 통한 정밀의료 기반 마련
score.reason: MFDS의 핵심 과제인 CKD 연구와 다중오믹스(대사체학) 통합, 임상 샘플 활용이 일치하나, EHR/RWD 데이터 기반이 없고 대규모 코호트/바이오뱅크 연계 없어 부분적 관련성만 있음.
